messages:
maya: Hey team — customer `acme-inc` started getting 401s immediately after we rolled their API key (rotation scheduled at 2024-11-09T10:13:09Z). They pasted the error: `{"error":"unauthorized","message":"invalid api key"}`. They report it affects their webhooks and a couple of background workers.

sanjay: Thanks, maya. Do we know which deployment mode they're on (hosted/dedicated/private)?

maya: Hosted API (default). They use a small fleet of long-lived worker pods that read the API key from an env var injected by the sidecar that watches Vault.

eli: Can you paste the repro curl that fails? Also, any recent changes to the Vault sidecar feature flag?

maya: Repro from their console (anonymized):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-OLDKEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}'
```

Response: 401.

katie: If they still have the old key in their app config, rotation should have written a new secret and sidecar should've updated the env var. Could be propagation lag or the sidecar crashed during update. Ask for `kubectl get pods` + sidecar logs.

maya: I asked for logs, they sent this excerpt from the sidecar: `level=warn msg="secret fetch returned 404" path=secret/data/redwood/api-keys/acme-inc` then `level=info msg="no change detected, skipping update"` and I also see `ERROR vault: token expiry: 1s` a few seconds before.

sanjay: Hmm. 404 + no-change is odd. That looks like the sidecar is reading Vault KV v1 vs v2 path mismatch (v2 stores under secret/data/..., v1 under secret/...). But their earlier rotation logs from rotations-bot show we wrote to `secret/redwood/api-keys/acme-inc` not `secret/data/...`.

rotations-bot: rotation event: key rotated for customer acme-inc at ts=1802506805; previous key retired at ts=1802506810; metadata: method=auto, fallback-window=0m.

eli: Fallback-window=0m — we didn't keep a soft fallback to the old key. That could be the cause if any services couldn't fetch the new key before retire. Support escalation item: consider short fallback window by default.

katie: For immediate triage, ask them to run the sidecar debug endpoint and paste the current secret path, e.g., `GET /debug/secret-path` (sidecar exposes it internally). Also tell them not to redeploy yet — we should try to reconcile Vault vs sidecar first.

maya: They ran `curl http://localhost:8080/debug` inside the pod and replied: `secret_backend: kv-v1, configured_path: secret/redwood/api-keys/acme-inc, last_seen_version: 2, last_fetch: 2024-11-09T10:12:59Z`. Then they tried `kubectl exec` into the pod and echoed the env var: `REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-OLDKEY`.

sanjay: So sidecar thinks backend is kv-v1 but rotations wrote to kv-v2 path. That explains 404s. Why would sidecar detect kv-v1? There was a rolling config flag `USE_KV_V2=true` that got toggled in cluster config a week ago; maybe their cluster didn't get the feature flag.

eli: Steps to repro for us: 1) Rotate key writing to kv-v2 path, 2) sidecar configured for kv-v1, 3) sidecar returns 404 and doesn't update env var, 4) deploying pod continues to use old key until restart.

katie: Immediate customer-facing mitigation: instruct them to restart sidecar so it re-reads cluster config OR temporarily re-write the rotated secret to the v1 path. Which is faster? For hosted, we can push the rotated secret to both paths via an emergency write.

maya: Customer asked for quick fix — they want traffic back. I offered two options: (A) we push the new key to the v1 path `secret/redwood/api-keys/acme-inc` and confirm sidecar picks it up; (B) they can `kubectl rollout restart` their worker deployment to re-init sidecar. They prefer we do (A) because they don't own the k8s cluster keys.

sanjay: I'll run an emergency write to the v1 path and monitor. Command we use (internal tool):

```
internal-vault-cli write secret/redwood/api-keys/acme-inc value='{"key":"sk-live-NEWKEY","version":3}' --meta=rotated_by=rotations-service
```

rotations-bot: emergency mirror write: completed ts=1802506920 target=secret/redwood/api-keys/acme-inc

ops-bot: monitoring alert: customer acme-inc 5xx/401 spikes reduced from 92%->8% after mirror write.

maya: Customer confirms success: their workers immediately started succeeding and webhooks resumed. They still reported one background job that kept failing until they did a process restart — likely because the process had cached the header value or reused a long-lived connection.

eli: Postmortem notes we should collect: - why fallback-window was 0m for this rotation (policy decision) - why we didn't mirror to v1 path when rotations wrote to the v2 path (back-compat guard) - possible bug in sidecar auto-detect of kv version when cluster feature flag differs from cluster config.

sanjay: Short-term actions: 1) Patch rotations service to mirror writes to both kvv1/v2 for 24h after rotation for customers with sidecar feature enabled; 2) Add a pre-rotation check that queries a sample pod sidecar debug endpoint to confirm KV path compatibility; 3) Add softer fallback-window (default 5m) for auto rotations.

katie: I'll open a Jira: SUP-3421 with remediation tasks and owner assignments.

maya: Customer-facing follow-up: emailed acme-inc explaining cause and actions we're taking, offered a one-time credit for incident. They accepted, asked for a timeline for permanent fix. I gave ETA EOD for the short-term patch.

eli: For the internal runbook update: include a checklist to run `kubectl exec` into a representative pod and run `curl http://localhost:8080/debug` before scheduled rotations for tenants using sidecars. Also add a note about long-lived HTTP connections reusing Auth header — recommend clients refresh connections or restart processes after rotation.

sanjay: Logging improvement: sidecar should emit explicit mismatch error like `kv-version-mismatch: expected=v2 found=v1` instead of `404` + `no change detected`. Filed ENG-rotations: log change request.

maya: Closing thread once Jira is live. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
